rules: Any liquid asset: stock, crypto, or leveraged/inverse ETF

positions.name: Direxion Daily S&P 500 Bull 3X Shares
positions.sector: Leveraged ETF — 3x Long S&P 500 (Broad US Large-Cap)
positions.catalyst: Broad risk-on melt-up to fresh record highs: S&P 500 and Dow at all-time highs (+0.6%) with ~90% of reporting companies beating estimates, and oil falling hard as President Trump signaled a Strait of Hormuz reopening deal could land as early as today — a clean macro tailwind (lower energy costs, geopolitical de-escalation) that broadens the rally beyond tech. Eli Lilly crossed a $1T cap on a Q2 beat, adding to the broad-based earnings strength lifting the tape.
positions.driver: LONG SPXL (3x S&P 500), 100% capital. Today's leadership is BROAD/cyclical, not tech-concentrated: Dow & S&P print new highs while the Nasdaq only digests tech earnings. Chose SPXL over TQQQ/SOXL because the day's soft spot is exactly semis/mega-cap tech — AMD is -6.5% (sell-the-news despite a double-beat + strong guide) and SpaceX -9% on its first public print, dragging on the Nasdaq. SPXL captures the record-high momentum + the Hormuz oil-down tailwind across 500 names with far more downside protection than a semis (SOXL) or Nasdaq (TQQQ) vehicle exposed to today's AMD/semis wobble. Entry only ~+0.8% on the day (SPXL 296.95 vs 294.56 close) — NOT extended, no chase. Stop 267.25 (-10%, matched to 3x). Runners-up: TQQQ (passed — Nasdaq lagging on AMD/SpaceX drag); SOXS 3x-inverse semis (passed — AMD weak but NVDA holding and fighting a record-high risk-on tape is low-edge); LLY (passed — extended after $1T milestone, no clean leveraged vehicle).
positions.risks: 3x magnifies reversals; a broad market already at record highs is vulnerable to a sharp mean-reversion or profit-taking day, and the Hormuz 'deal close' headline could disappoint/reverse (oil spikes back, risk-off) and gap SPXL toward the 267.25 stop. A hot macro print (jobs/inflation) or a deepening AMD-led semis rout spilling into the broad index are the key risks. Mitigants: 500-name diversification cushions single-stock gap risk (vs SOXL/TQQQ), entry is not chased (+0.8% on day), broad 90% beat rate + oil-down macro skews the read-through bullish, hard 10% stop + daily rotation cap loss.
